market_summary: Global markets face mixed sentiment as tech giants navigate regulatory pressures and forecasts shift. Nvidia tightened chip tracking in Southeast Asia to combat smuggling concerns, while Tesla announced winding down Cybertruck production by mid-2027 to focus on Cybercab robotaxis. Singapore's banking sector showed resilience with OCBC beating earnings estimates; DBS and UOB missed expectations but analysts see buying opportunities after recent sell-offs. US equity markets await inflation data and earnings clarity. Singapore Airlines faces further delays on its S$2 billion cabin retrofit programme, now pushed to H2 2027 due to aircraft certification issues.

items.headline: Nvidia requires Southeast Asian cloud partners to enroll in Fleet Intelligence chip tracking system
items.summary: <cite index="1-3">Nvidia requires customers in Southeast Asia to enroll in its Fleet Intelligence system tracking AI accelerators' location to become official Nvidia Cloud Partners</cite>, as <cite index="2-3">US officials believe Chinese firms have bought billions of dollars of banned Nvidia processors through Southeast Asian smuggling networks</cite>.

items.headline: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production mid-2027 for Cybercab robotaxi production
items.summary: <cite index="12-4,12-5">Cybertruck production will be winding down to make room for the Cybercab, starting mid-2027</cite>. <cite index="16-8,16-9">Tesla sold 20,237 Cybertrucks last year, down about half from prior year, with sales through September down 28%</cite>.

items.headline: OCBC posts Q3 2026 net profit of S$2.04 billion, up 3% YoY; upgrades 2026 guidance
items.summary: <cite index="23-1">OCBC posted net profit of S$2.04 billion for Q3 2026, a 3% increase from S$1.98 billion a year earlier</cite>. <cite index="20-7,20-8">Banking Operations profit reached record S$1.90 billion, up 16% YoY, while net interest income rose 4% to S$2.31 billion, the highest in six quarters</cite>. <cite index="20-12">OCBC upgraded 2026 guidance on loan growth, total income and credit costs</cite>.

items.headline: DBS and UOB miss Q3 earnings estimates amid analyst target cuts; OCBC beats expectations
items.summary: <cite index="22-2,22-3">DBS and UOB miss Q3 earnings estimates as Singapore banking heavyweights fell during results week amid renewed caution on earnings outlook</cite>. <cite index="33-4">Three brokers rate DBS a buy with targets of S$79.50 to S$86.80</cite>, suggesting analysts still see upside despite recent weakness.

items.headline: Singapore Airlines delays new A350 cabin retrofit to H2 2027 due to seat certification issues
items.summary: <cite index="41-1,41-8">Singapore Airlines delays new First and Business Class to H2 2027; both new seats are certified on 777-9 but still await A350 certification</cite>. <cite index="42-4,42-6,42-7">Unveiling arrives amid persistent delays; A350 certification delay pushed back introduction by about half a year</cite>.

items.headline: Ex-ST Engineering and Singtel executive Low Ka Hoe to become Netlink NBN Trust CEO
items.summary: Low Ka Hoe, a former executive at ST Engineering and Singtel, will succeed Tong Yew Heng as CEO of Netlink NBN Trust, signalling management transition at the Singapore telecommunications infrastructure provider.

items.headline: Google executive Donald Harrison resigns from SpaceX board
items.summary: A Google executive has resigned from SpaceX's board, reflecting ongoing separation between the two companies amid various tech industry board dynamics and strategic considerations.
